doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Pay, health and the Gibson guitar
title: The Gibson Herb Ellis guitar
summary: Ellis talks about having a Gibson model named for him, based on the ES 175 he played since 1953 but built of real wood.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: I want to ask you about what it must feel like to have a guitar named after you.

Oh, that’s a real great feeling. And even better is a lot of people like the guitar and they buy it, not in the same way that they’d buy a rock guitar, but it does pretty well for guitarists. And I’m very proud of the fact. It makes you feel great, it really does.
How did the Gibson company, what questions did they ask you in building the guitar?

They asked me, you know, what style I wanted. And they had a guitar that I played since 1953 that mine is very similar. That was an ES 175, and they called mine the Herb Ellis ES 165. And the only difference really is that the ES 175 is made out of plywood and mine is made out of real wood you know. It’s just a better quality guitar. And it’s pretty reasonable too.
